Population totals from the frame behind a sample

Source: R/survey.R
frame_totals.Rd

Totals the columns of the frame a sample was drawn from, as stored with the sample, in the form survey::calibrate() takes as population. A design handed over by as_svydesign() can then be calibrated, or post-stratified, to the frame without building the totals by hand.

Usage

frame_totals(sample, formula, table = FALSE)

Arguments

sample

A data frame returned by draw() with weights = TRUE.

formula

A one-sided formula of frame columns, such as ~ w + site, as survey::calibrate() takes it. A name in it that is not a column of the frame, such as cutoff in ~ I(w > cutoff), is read from the environment of formula, as stats::model.frame() reads it. A term with no frame column in it, as in ~ cutoff, has no value for each row and is refused, and so is one that gives a single value for the frame, such as I(sum(w)).

table

FALSE, the default, for the column totals of the model matrix of formula, which survey::calibrate() takes. TRUE for the count of rows in each cell of the variables in formula, as a table, which survey::postStratify() and survey::rake() take.

Value

With table = FALSE, a named numeric vector: the totals of the columns of model.matrix(formula) over the rows the design could reach, (Intercept) being the number of those rows. With table = TRUE, a table of counts of those rows from stats::xtabs().

Details

The totals run over the rows the design could have drawn, those with an inclusion probability above 0 when the sample was drawn: the rows inside the region of design_spatial() or the window of design_temporal(), those design_reservoir() read before max_items, and not the rows na_rm dropped. Those are the rows the sample's weights stand for. For a sample weighted conditional on the clusters selected (see "Design weights" in draw()), the rows of the clusters left out count too, since another selection could have drawn them. A missing value of a variable in formula in any of those rows is refused, since its total is unknown.

A value of a column in formula that no sampled row has cannot be calibrated to. survey::calibrate() stops on such a factor level, and leaves out the total of such a character value with a warning that it reordered the totals. Calibration itself is left to survey, which gives the calibrated estimates their standard errors.

See also

as_svydesign()

Examples

pop <- data.frame(
  id = 1:400,
  site = rep(c("a", "b", "c", "d"), times = c(200, 100, 60, 40)),
  size = 20 + (1:400 * 53) %% 300
)
pop$spend <- 3 * pop$size + (1:400 * 37) %% 90
s <- draw(pop, design_simple(n = 60), seed = 1, weights = TRUE)
des <- as_svydesign(s)

# Calibrate to the frame's row count and total size
totals <- frame_totals(s, ~size)
totals
#> (Intercept)        size 
#>         400       67300 
cal <- survey::calibrate(des, ~size, population = totals)
survey::svytotal(~spend, cal)
#>        total     SE
#> spend 218918 1238.9
ht_total(s, "spend")
#> Horvitz-Thompson total  (simple design, n = 60)
#>   estimate 219,173.3
#>   se       12,239.06  (analytic)
#>   95% CI  194,683 to 243,663.6  (t, 59 df)
#>   deff     1  (about the same as simple random sampling)

# Post-stratify on site
counts <- frame_totals(s, ~site, table = TRUE)
post <- survey::postStratify(des, ~site, counts)
survey::svytotal(~spend, post)
#>        total    SE
#> spend 219786 12124
